ad_ranking.note: Tiers compare ads across ad groups, so search intent shows up as well as copy; the head-to-heads are the copy verdict. Tier needs 100+ impressions and 20+ clicks.

ad_strength_vs_results.finding: Inside ad groups the stronger-rated ad won on CTR in 3 of 3 head-to-heads and on conversions per impression in 3 of 3, but only one of those CTR gaps is clear. Across ad groups strength predicts little: the top-ranked ad is rated AVERAGE, and the EXCELLENT band holds one ad with 33 impressions, too few to judge. Use strength as a completeness check, not a performance score.

line_ranking.note: One impression shows several lines, so lines are compared, never added up within an ad. Click index = clicks / (impressions x the ad's CTR) x 100; it needs 100+ line impressions. Google's per-line ratings came back PENDING or LEARNING on most lines and GOOD on a few; none BEST or LOW.

angles.weak_headlines_note: Service-only headlines: feature-only names the service and nothing else; generic names no service at all. A pattern is a flag, not a verdict: the line's verdict still comes from its numbers.
angles.finding: Proof and question headlines earn more clicks than their ads' average when shown (index 130 and 119); availability lines earn fewer (93). No angle has fewer than 3 distinct headlines, so there are no gaps, but proof is spread thin: 7 proof headlines against 20 location headlines.

descriptions.note: Every non-brand serving description, by exact text. Checks: short (under 80 of the 90 characters), no call to action (no sentence starts with an action verb or says call now, us or today), no proof, offer or pain point (no reason to choose this business). Character counts are of the real text before anonymising.
